paper_title: Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners A Comprehensive   Evaluation and Beyond
caption: Visualization on the metric of answer correctness.
model_annotation: This 3D bar chart visualizes the accuracy of three large language models—Davinci-03, ChatGPT, and BARD—across three distinct reasoning types: Inductive, Deductive, and Mix, with a fourth category labeled “Abductive” appearing to be a mislabeling or error in the chart’s x-axis labeling, as it is not aligned with the other reasoning types. The vertical axis represents “Accuracy,” scaled linearly from 0 to 0.8, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The horizontal axis is labeled with the model names (Davinci-03, ChatGPT, BARD) along the front edge and the reasoning types (Inductive, Deductive, Mix) along the side, though the spatial arrangement suggests the reasoning types are the primary categorical variable. Each bar’s height corresponds to the accuracy score for that model under that reasoning type. The bars are colored with a gradient from blue (lower values) to yellow (higher values), visually indicating the relative accuracy. The tallest bars, representing the highest accuracy scores, are for ChatGPT under the “Inductive” and “Mix” reasoning types, reaching approximately 0.8. The shortest bars, representing the lowest accuracy scores, are for BARD under the “Inductive” reasoning type, with an accuracy of approximately 0.1. The bars are not sorted in any particular order, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond the color gradient.
